content.title: Trump shifts focus to housing: What comes next?
content.summary: Investing.com -- President Trump has turned housing policy into a political priority ahead of the midterm elections, with TD Cowen saying the White House is now targeting institutional landlords, down-payment access and mortgage fees as part of a broad affordability push.

content.title: What kind of federal policies will bring US home prices down?
content.description:
As mortgage rates tick lower in the first week of 2026, President Trump has called for Fannie Mae (FNMA) and Freddie Mac (FMCC) to acquire more mortgage bonds.

Redfin chief economist Daryl Fairweather discusses what kinds of federal policies could effectively lower US home prices.

content.title: Trump Wants Fannie, Freddie to Buy More Mortgage Bonds. Here’s Why.
content.summary: 0.25% or more   That's how much mortgage rates could fall if Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac buy more mortgage bonds, according to National Housing Conference Chief Executive David Dworkin.   Late Thursday, President Trump said the two government-backed companies would buy $200 billion's worth of mortgage bonds, as part of a push to make home ownership more affordable.

content.title: Trump says 'representatives' will buy $200B in mortgage bonds
content.description:
President Trump said in a social media post on Thursday that he is "instructing representatives" to buy $200 billion in mortgage bonds, which he says will lower monthly payments and make home ownership more affordable.

ResiClub co-founder and CEO Lance Lambert explains what this would mean for home buyers, telling Asking for a Trend host Josh Lipton that it may not make a huge dent in the housing affordability crisis.
